subject: english-language
title: Accents and Dialects
welcome_lead: English sounds different in every town. Why?
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on accents vs dialects across regions.
final_note: You can now tell accent from dialect with regional examples.

concepts.def: Speech tied to a social group.
An individual's own way of speaking.

walkthroughs.body_html: A Geordie speaker may say 'barm' (dialect word) in a Geordie accent (sound). Dialect is words + grammar; accent is sound.
Received Pronunciation (RP) is a non-regional, prestigious accent — often heard in older BBC broadcasts.
A sociolect is the speech of a group (teen slang). An idiolect is your own personal mix of speech habits.

mcqs.q: Your own personal way of speaking is your.
What does Labov's research show about language variation?
options: Labov showed that working-class people speak ungrammatically.
Language varies systematically by social class, gender, age and context — and speakers shift style depending on formality, often unconsciously.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Labov showed that everyone speaks the same way regardless of background.

mcqs.q: Why does English vocabulary have so many synonyms?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
English has many synonyms because Shakespeare invented lots of words.
Because English speakers have always wanted to make things complicated.
Layered historical contact — Old English, Old Norse, Norman French and Latin — left English with multiple words from different sources for similar concepts (e.g. ask/question/interrogate).
